findings.claim: `tidewater book` accepts a vessel into a berth too shallow for it (for example Razorbill, draught 2.6 m, into B1, max 1.5 m): src/cli.js checks only that the vessel, berth and window exist. No obligation in this arc adds the draught refusal, because the census marks T-13 and T-14 out-of-slice. The arc advances V-3 and V-4 and will send a confirmation text for this booking, so the skipper only finds out on the quay that the berth cannot take her.

`cancel` in src/ledger.js splices the booking out of the ledger and keeps no record of the cancellation. Any cancellation made under this design is lost to the harbour master's morning view (V-6 needs 'anything cancelled overnight'). berth-clash is about to rework the ledger shape for I-10, which is the cheap moment to keep cancellations as records instead of deleting them.

I-2 dates a window by its high water, and the exact confirmation template prints only {date} and the window times. A booking for the 2026-10-08 00:21 high water would therefore read 'on 2026-10-08 … (window 22:51-01:51)', but that window opens at 22:51 on 2026-10-07. A skipper reading the text in a hurry could arrive a day late, which is the surprise on the quay V-3 rules out. The vision does not foresee this case, and changing the template needs the harbour master's agreement (T-58).

The corpus defines a booking by two windows, but the exact confirmation template has room for only one: T-149 (0030_Bookings.md:11) says a booking names "the tide window it arrives on and the tide window it leaves on", with the example "from the 20:31 high water on 4 October to the 08:57 high water on 5 October" (line 7). The "Booking confirmed" template that T-55 requires word for word (message-templates.md:12,20) has a single {date} and {hw}, so a confirmation cannot say when the booking ends, and T-58 says the wording cannot change without the harbour master.

`tidewater list <date>` in src/ledger.js:107 now keeps only bookings that arrive on that date, so a boat that arrived the day before and stays through the given date is left off the day's list. That is the list the office prints each morning and pins by the radio (T-76) and the one the harbour master checks against the register each evening (T-78), so a berth that is held shows as empty to the people who place boats by hand on the quay (T-82, T-111).

src/ledger.js never breaks a stale `<ledger>.lock`. If a book or cancel dies without reaching its finally block (a kill or a power cut on the office machine whose disk the kiosk shares), every later booking from the kiosk is refused, and the refusal only says to ask the office. No corpus page or operations routine tells the office what to do about the lock, so skippers are sent back to phoning the harbour office.

docs/corpus/0010_Overview.md:37 still documents the command as "`book <vessel> <berth> <date> <hw>` books a berth for the window around a high water". But src/cli.js:37 now refuses that four-argument form and requires `book <vessel> <berth> <date> <hw> <leave-date> <leave-hw>`. The audited range changed the command without changing the corpus page that describes it, which T-5 forbids ("A change to how Tidewater behaves changes the document that describes it in the same go"). The code is right per T-149; the document is stale.

The clash check in src/ledger.js treats each tide window as a separate slot ordered by `date hw`. On the audited tide table, though, the 23:47 window on 2026-10-07 (22:17–01:17) and the 00:21 window on 2026-10-08 (22:51–01:51) overlap in real time. B3 can therefore be booked to one vessel leaving on the first and another arriving on the second, and the I-6 witness 'a berth is free again after the window its booking leaves on' asserts that this pair of bookings succeeds.

Bookings can now span several windows, but `list <date>` in src/ledger.js still filters only on the arrival date. A boat that arrives on 2026-10-04 and stays to 2026-10-06 is left off the 2026-10-05 list, which the office prints each morning (T-76) and the harbour master checks against the berths (T-78).

The I-2 witnesses (tides.test.js:12-14 and 22-26) never check that a window opening before midnight is refused under the date it opens on: they never call windowOf('2026-10-07', '00:21'). So windowOf in src/tides.js:27-31 could also accept a window under the previous date and the lane would stay green, even though `book Puffin B1 2026-10-07 00:21 ...` would then be stored under a second key that the ledger's clash check (ledger.js `at(date, window)`) never compares with '2026-10-08 00:21'.

In src/cli.js:44-46, `book` writes the confirmation text to the outbox only after the booking has been saved to the ledger and the lock released, and prints the `booked bk-n` line only after that. If the outbox write fails (folder unwritable or disk full on the shared office disk), the command crashes with a stack trace even though the booking stands. The skipper gets no text, never sees her booking id, and is likely to think the booking failed.

The audited range added src/texts.js and src/outbox.js and made `book` write a confirmation text, but the Modules list in docs/corpus/0050_Architecture.md:29-33 still names only cli.js, tides.js, registers.js, ledger.js and errors.js, and the `book` entry in docs/corpus/0010_Overview.md:37 still says nothing about the text. T-5 requires the opposite: "A change to how Tidewater behaves changes the document that describes it in the same go". The code is right per T-43 and T-50; the architecture document is what is stale.

`list <date>` in src/ledger.js:112 picks bookings by the tide-table date of their arrival and leaving windows, but the clash check (ledger.js:66,84) now counts the real clock time a berth is held. So `list 2026-10-07` leaves out a boat booked on the 2026-10-08 00:21 high water, even though her window opens at 22:51 on 2026-10-07, and `list 2026-10-08` leaves out a boat that leaves on the 2026-10-07 23:47 window and holds the berth until 01:17 on 2026-10-08.

The taken-berth refusal in src/ledger.js:88 always says the berth is booked to the other vessel "until" that vessel's leaving window. When the overlap comes from a midnight-spanning window, or from a booking that starts later than the one asked for, the line contradicts the request: a skipper who asks for B3 on the 2026-10-08 00:21 window is told 'B3 is booked to Puffin until the 23:47 high water on 2026-10-07', a time before the window she asked for, and nothing says the two windows overlap.

The audited range made Tidewater refuse an over-draught booking at booking time (src/cli.js:42 calls checkDraught), but docs/corpus/0020_Berths.md:73-74 still says "Today the harbour master does this check by eye, each evening on the next day's list; Tidewater should do it at the moment of booking". T-5 requires the describing document to change "in the same go", and the range touched only README.md. The code is right per T-13 and T-14; the corpus page is stale.

checkDraught in src/registers.js:26 compares Math.round(draught*10) with Math.round(maxDraught*10), which rounds the vessel's draught to the nearest tenth. T-12 says a draught is "rounded up to the next tenth of a metre" and T-14 refuses a vessel that "draws more than the berth's maximum draught". So a register entry such as 1.54 m would be accepted into B1 (max 1.5 m). The data/vessels.json entries all have one decimal today, so nothing is affected yet.

The audited range adds the test 'a booking whose text cannot be written still shows its booking id' (test/unit/booking.test.js:101-113). It pins as intended behaviour a booking that stays in the ledger with no confirmation text, and the command then crashes. That contradicts I-11 / T-43 (0040_Notifications.md:13): "Every booking whose vessel has a phone number writes its confirmation text to the outbox as the booking is made". src/cli.js:45-47 commits the booking before it calls sendBookingConfirmation, so a failed outbox write leaves a booking with no text.

The I-13 witness 'a vessel with no phone number gets no text' (test/unit/texts.test.js:34-48) never runs the book command. It calls sendBookingConfirmation directly with a made-up record {name:'NoPhone'} that the real path could never deliver, because checkDraught (src/registers.js:23) refuses a vessel with no draught before cli.js:47 is reached. Every vessel in data/vessels.json has a phone, so no unit test sends a phone-less registered vessel through `tidewater book`, and a CLI change that texts such a vessel leaves the lane green.

`tidewater cancel <booking>` (src/cli.js:53-56, src/ledger.js:103-110) removes whichever booking matches the sequential id it is given. It does not check the vessel and does not tell the holder, so a mistyped or guessed bk-n at the kiosk or office silently frees another skipper's berth for rebooking, even though she holds a confirmation text saying the berth is hers.

The audited range guards `tidewater cancel` with the booking's vessel name (src/ledger.js:108), but the name is no secret. `tidewater list`, which anyone at the kiosk can run, prints every booking id next to its vessel (src/cli.js:51), and the taken-berth refusal names the holder (src/ledger.js:92). So anyone at the kiosk can still free another skipper's berth, the holder is not told, and she arrives holding a confirmation text for a berth that someone else has since booked.

The audited range changed `cancel` to require the vessel and to refuse a mismatch (src/cli.js:54, src/ledger.js:103-110), but the corpus that describes the command was not updated. docs/corpus/0010_Overview.md:40 still says "`cancel <booking>` cancels one", and T-38 (docs/corpus/0030_Bookings.md:66) still says "Cancelling takes the booking id", with no rule for the new vessel check or its refusal. T-5 requires the describing document to change "in the same go"; only README.md changed.

When a booking is refused because the berth is taken (src/ledger.js:92), the message ends with a generic 'pick another berth or another window'. It names no berth that is free for that stay and no window that is free for that berth. So a skipper turned away at the kiosk has to guess and retry, or phone the office, to find something she can book. T-4 says she should be told what she could book instead.

`tidewater cancel` in src/ledger.js:103-114 removes a booking at any time, even after its window has opened. T-35 (docs/corpus/0030_Bookings.md:63) says the opposite: "A skipper may cancel a booking until 24 hours before its tide window opens; after that the cancellation is refused and the berth stays booked". So a late cancellation frees a berth the corpus says must stay booked, and another skipper can book it.

src/outbox.js:10-12 names each text `<booking id>-<pid>-<random uuid>.txt` and nothing in the file says when it was written, so when the gateway is down (T-51) a booking's confirmation and the cancellation that cli.js:57 now writes for the same bk-n wait side by side with no order between them; the gateway can send them in either order, and a skipper whose last text reads 'is booked into berth' may sail in to a berth that went back to the pool.

The audited range adds the test 'a cancellation whose text cannot be written still shows it went through' (test/unit/booking.test.js:171-182), which pins as intended behaviour a cancellation that is committed to the ledger while no cancellation text is written and the command crashes. This contradicts T-44 (0040_Notifications.md:22): "Every cancellation that goes through, for a vessel with a phone number, writes a cancellation text to the outbox". The cause is src/cli.js:55-57, which commits cancel() and prints the line before it calls sendBookingCancellation.

The I-26 witness 'every outbox text is about a booking in the ledger' (test/unit/texts.test.js:212-222) only runs `book`. It never sees the cancellation texts this range adds (src/cli.js:57, src/texts.js), and it could not judge them if it did: `cancel` splices the booking out of the ledger (src/ledger.js:111), and the cancellation template has no 'Ref bk-n.' line for the witness's regex to match. So no I-26 witness reaches the cancel path that now writes texts.

`cancel` in src/ledger.js:113-114 now puts the cancellation text in the outbox (through cli.js:55 and outbox.js:14) before it saves the ledger, so if the save fails (for example a full or unwritable shared disk) the skipper gets a text saying 'is cancelled. The berth is free again.' while the ledger still holds her booking and the command crashes with no output.

src/ledger.js:111-114 now publishes the cancellation text to the outbox (beforeSave → writeText, which renames into the outbox at src/outbox.js:14) before save(ledger). If the ledger write then fails (for example a full or unwritable shared disk), the booking stays in the ledger while the gateway sends 'booking bk-n … is cancelled. The berth is free again.' (src/texts.js:10). That contradicts T-44 (0040_Notifications.md:22), which ties the text to 'Every cancellation that goes through', and the new README:23 line, which says the cancellation goes through only with its text and that 'otherwise the booking stands'.

`cancel` in src/ledger.js:113-114 now publishes the cancellation text to the outbox (beforeSave → writeText's renameSync at src/outbox.js:14) before it calls save(ledger). If the ledger write then fails, for example a full or unwritable shared disk, the command crashes and the booking stays in the ledger, but a text telling the skipper 'is cancelled. The berth is free again.' (src/texts.js:10) is already waiting for the gateway.
